plan.title: sec: issue ingest leaves title/plan.items unscanned; scope lifecycle follows xbrief folder symlinks

narratives.Description: This story implements the cited GitHub issue acceptance criteria in the scoped packages listed in swarm.file_scope. It includes regression tests and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased Fixed or Changed as appropriate.
narratives.Overview:
**Severity:** Medium (2 findings)
**Source:** Scheduled application-security review at `6e288a2de499cadfce43e176a7b08c5d15d52d4f`
**Related:** incomplete coverage after #2306 (issue ingest quarantine); same symlink trust-boundary class as #2413 / #2446 / #2383

## Summary

Two further medium findings from the same AppSec pass:

1. Issue ingest still leaves `plan.title` and derived `plan.items[].title` unscanned after #2306 quarantined Overview.
2. Scope lifecycle transitions can relocate story xBRIEFs outside the checkout when a lifecycle folder under `xbrief/` is a repo-controlled symlink.

---

### 1) Medium — Issue ingest leaves title and `plan.items` unscanned after #2306

**Location:** `packages/core/src/lifecycle/issue-ingest.ts`

**Attacker / input:** an attacker opens a GitHub issue with an injection-shaped or credential-shaped title and/or checkbox acceptance-criteria lines. An empty body can skip the body scan entirely.

**Attack path:**
1. Maintainer runs `triage:accept` / `issue:ingest`.
2. `buildIssueVbrief` scans only Overview (post-#2306).
3. Prompt-injection / credential-shaped text persists into agent-authoritative xBRIEF fields: `plan.title`, `narratives.Description`, and `plan.items[].title`.

**Impact:** quarantined Overview creates a false sense of safety while title and checkbox AC text still land in fields agents treat as authoritative.

**Remediation:** run `scan()` on the issue title and each extracted plan-item title (fail closed on hard-fail; fence soft signals) before writing the xBRIEF; prefer scanning derived fields from transformed content.

---

### 2) Medium — Scope lifecycle moves follow symlinked `xbrief` folder targets outside the repo

**Location:** `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts`

**Attacker / input:** a malicious repository author commits a lifecycle folder such as `xbrief/completed` (or another lifecycle directory) as a symlink to a writable path outside the checkout.

**Attack path:**
1. Victim runs a routine lifecycle verb such as `task scope:complete` (also promote / activate).
2. Transition code calls `mkdirSync` + `renameSync` on the destination under `xbrief/<lifecycle>/`.
3. Those calls follow the folder symlink and relocate the story xBRIEF outside the project tree.

**Impact:** scope lifecycle can move story artifacts into an attacker-chosen directory outside the checkout under the victim account.

**Remediation:** apply `assertProjectionContained` (or equivalent `lstat` / `realpath` containment) to lifecycle destination dirs before mkdir/rename; reject escaping folder symlinks.

---

## Acceptance

- [ ] `issue:ingest` / `triage:accept` runs quarantine `scan()` on issue title and each derived `plan.items[].title` before writing the xBRIEF; hard-fail refuses the write; soft signals are fenced.
- [ ] Empty-body issues still scan title (and any extracted plan-item titles); body-scan skip does not imply title/item skip.
- [ ] `scope:complete` / `promote` / `activate` refuse when the destination lifecycle folder (or a parent under `xbrief/`) is a symlink or resolves outside the project root; no out-of-tree `mkdir`/`rename` occurs.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: injection-shaped title + checkbox AC into xBRIEF fields; empty-body title-only path; symlink-at-lifecycle-folder and symlink-in-parent-path for scope transitions.

## Notes

Finding (1) is a residual gap on #2306 — prefer extending the existing ingest scanner rather than a parallel path. Finding (2) should reuse `#2413` / `#2446` containment (`assertProjectionContained`) on lifecycle destinations; can ship with or immediately after the triage-cache / init-deposit containment work in #2446.

narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer ingesting issues, I want titles and plan items quarantined and scope moves contained, so that injection text and symlink escapes cannot land outside trusted boundaries.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an injection-shaped issue title or checkbox AC, when issue:ingest runs, then hard-fail refuses or soft signals are fenced before write.
Given an empty body, when ingest runs, then title and extracted item titles are still scanned.
Given a symlinked xbrief lifecycle folder, when scope promote/activate/complete runs, then the transition refuses out-of-tree rename.
